questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The radius of the Earth is \( 6400 $\mathrm{ km}$\). If the height of the antenna is \( 500 $\mathrm{ m}$\) then its range is
questions.solution:
Given, radius of Earth, $R=6400 \mathrm{ km}$; height of antenna $=500 \mathrm{ m}=500 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{ km}$
Now, range of antenna $=\sqrt{2 R h}=\sqrt{2 \times 6400} \times 500 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{ km}=\sqrt{64 \times 100}=80 \mathrm{ km}$
Therefore, range of antenna $=80 \mathrm{ km}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
\( 4 \times10^{10} \) electrons are removed from a neutral metal sphere of diameter \( 20 $\mathrm{ cm}$\) placed in air.
The magnitude of the electric field (in \( N C^{-1} \) ) at a distance of \( 20 $\mathrm{ cm}$\) from its centre is:
questions.solution:
Given, number of electrons removed $=4 \times 10^{10}$; diameter of metal sphere $=20 \mathrm{ cm}$; distance $\mathrm{r}=20 \mathrm{ cm}$. Therefore,
Electric field $=\frac{1}{4 \Pi \varepsilon_{0}} \frac{q}{r^{2}}$
where $\frac{1}{4 \Pi \varepsilon_{0}}=9 \times 10^{9}\Rightarrow q=\left(4 \times 10^{10}\right) \times\left(1.6 \times 10^{-19}\right)=6.4 \times 10^{-9}$
Electric field
$=\frac{9 \times 10^{9} \times 6.4 \times 10^{-9}}{\left(20 \times 10^{-2}\right)^{2}}=1440 \mathrm{ N} \mathrmC^{-1}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A stone of mass \( 0.05 $\mathrm{ kg}$\) is thrown vertically upwards. What is the direction and magnitude of
net force on the stone during its upward motion?
questions.solution:
Given, mass $\mathrm{m}=0.05 \mathrm{ kg}$
When the stone is thrown upwards, force due to gravity acts on the stone vertically downwards, it is given as
$F=m g=0.05 \times 9.8=0.49$
Magnitude of net force $=0.49 \mathrm{ N}$
Direction of net force is vertically downwards.
